lines.text: Xenoform turns a song into a music video.
One object turns into the next, on the beat, for the whole song.
It runs on your own computer, with open-weight models through ComfyUI.
This is the whole tour: the song, the vibe, what it morphs through, the render, the edit, your own clips, and how it's built.
Start with a song.
Drop a file on the page, or use the bundled demo.
The desk listens first.
It finds the beats, the bars and the drop, and tells you where the big moment is.
That's where the biggest change will land.
Then pick a vibe.
A vibe is what everything is made of and how it's lit: molten gold, neon noir, ink and paper, deep-sea glow, and more.
Each vibe brings its own objects, colour and transitions with it.
Pick None for the things as they really are, in their own materials and plain light.
Under the vibes is one line: what it morphs through.
It isn't a story prompt.
It names the things you want to see.
Type a few things, a theme, a place, or a feel.
A theme like underwater brings fifteen things of its own: a jellyfish, an octopus, a seahorse, a manta ray.
Name a place, and the morphs pass through it as a scene.
A feel, like moody and punchy, moves the knobs and the look.
The chips under the line show how it was read.
New means the still is drawn first, on your GPU, before the render.
The objects come from a library that grows on this machine.
Every still is made with Z-Image Turbo and checked against the vibe's own pool before it's kept.
Press Make.
The making screen shows the chain it picked, the steps, and a rough cut of the song playing while the morphs render.
You can leave it.
The tab counts up and tells you when it's ready.
There are four models.
A Draft renders small with LTX-Video, in minutes.
lines.say: A Draft renders small with LTX Video, in minutes.

lines.text: A Fast Final upscales the Draft to 1080p.
lines.say: A Fast Final upscales the Draft to ten eighty p.

lines.text: The Final renders every morph with LTX-2.5: sharp, and slow, a few minutes a morph on this card.
lines.say: The Final renders every morph with LTX 2.5: sharp, and slow, a few minutes a morph on this card.

lines.text: Cloud Final sends the same open-weights morphs to Comfy Cloud, three at a time, on your credits, when you tick the box.
The time row says how long it will take on this GPU, before you start.
Now the engine.
Morph style is how one object turns into the next.
Melt flows.
Shatter cracks into shards that snap together.
Bloom opens like a flower.
Spin turns as it changes.
Fold creases like paper.
Auto melts the verses and shatters the drop.
Timing is when the change happens inside the shot.
Smooth plays it evenly.
On the beat moves it in steps, on every beat.
Snap holds, then changes in about a beat, on the downbeat.
Effects ride the kick and the loudness: dither hits, a feedback tunnel, a kaleidoscope, slit-scan.
Any of them together.
Foreshadow lets the next object arrive early: its edges glow in, or strips of it flicker toward the cut.
Scenes mixes wide places in at each new section.
And four knobs.
Intensity for the pulse and the flash, Speed for how often it cuts, Chaos for the punches, Glow for the bloom.
None of this needs the GPU again.
Every change waits in one bar at the bottom, and Apply re-cuts the video from the morphs it already made.
Under the video is the timeline.
Every tile is a shot, with its own frame, and a playhead crosses it as the video plays.
Click a shot to open it.
The drawer has four tabs.
Shot: play it, move it left or right, duplicate it, or delete it.
The shot before plays on through the gap.
Look: colour for this shot alone, hue, saturation, brightness, contrast and warmth, and its own effects.
Join: the seam between two shots.
Flow or cut, the transition, and move the cut a beat or half a beat either way.
Regenerate: swap the object, change its morph style, render just this one morph again, or generate a new one here.
Edit as many shots as you like, then apply once.
It re-cuts from the cached morphs, without the GPU.
Morph has a second mode: clips.
Point it at a folder of your own footage, or the free film pack, and the cut is only clips, never mixed with objects.
Each clip plays its busiest stretch, at full speed.
Between clips, LTX generates a morph from the last frame of one into the first frame of the next.
Here, the Metropolis robot turns into A Trip to the Moon, the Moon into the dinosaurs of The Lost World, and the Odessa steps into Keaton's bridge.
All public domain, from the free film pack.
When it's done, share it: a small share cut, a fifteen-second hook for social, or the whole thing.
Edit in Resolve opens a folder with a timeline: one file a shot, the song, and markers, ready to import.
A recipe code remakes the same video anywhere.
And Variations queues extra Drafts for later: new objects, other vibes, other feels.
Under the hood.
First the song: it is split into stems with Demucs, and every beat and the drop are found in the mix.
This track: seventy beats in thirty seconds, the drop at thirteen point seven.
Then the plan: a shot on every bar, a half bar on the drop.
Here that is twenty-two shots, and the stems decide the effects on each: a punch on the downbeat, a stutter on the kick.
Then the chain: twenty-three stills, one object leading to the next.
Twelve came from the None library, three were drawn first for the line: a seashell, coral, a pearl oyster.
Each shot is one morph: the still it starts on, the still it ends on, and a prompt naming them both, asking for the change across the whole clip.
That graph goes to ComfyUI through the Comfy SDK, and LTX-2.5 renders it.
lines.say: That graph goes to ComfyUI through the Comfy SDK, and LTX 2.5 renders it.

lines.text: The morph comes back as a short video clip.
Xenoform re-times it so the change lands on the beat, runs the effects the knobs asked for on the stems, and cuts it all to the song.
Every step leaves a file in the job folder: the beats, the plan, the chain, every morph.
Nothing in it is a black box.
The plan becomes ComfyUI graphs, sent through the Comfy SDK to your own ComfyUI.
LTX-Video, LTX-2.5 and Z-Image Turbo do the work: all open weights, on any card from 12 GB up, or the same models on Comfy Cloud when you ask for Cloud Final.
lines.say: LTX Video, LTX 2.5 and Z Image Turbo do the work: all open weights, on any card from twelve gigabytes up, or the same models on Comfy Cloud when you ask for Cloud Final.

lines.text: And an MCP server lets any AI drive the desk: pick a vibe, render, review, and re-cut.
Setup and models asks your ComfyUI which models it can load, and offers a download for any it lacks.
Xenoform.
